thread:
eli: Proposal sketch: 1) Keep current API keys read-only for 90 days while we accept them at a bridge endpoint. 2) Bridge returns a short-lived mTLS cert or JWT (TTL = 1h) that the client uses for calls. 3) Console + CLI tool to rotate keys to OIDC/SAML-backed service identities. 4) Phased enforcement (warn -> opt-in -> required).

maria: +1 on having a clear bridge. can we make the bridge itself single-purpose and stateless? I'd prefer not to add another long-lived secret store if we can avoid it.

sam: Agree. Also need to think about offline devices / air-gapped customers. They might not be able to do the live exchange every hour. Maybe allow intermediate tokens with longer TTL for certified devices.

eli: Good call. We could support two migration modes: interactive (short TTL, OIDC) and device-assertion (signed CSR + longer TTL cert issued after vetting). Documented and opt-in per tenant.

julie: How do we revoke in emergencies? If someone leaks an old API key we want quick revocation. Does the bridge keep a denylist?

eli: Bridge will consult central revocation service (existing KMS/audit subsystem) — we already have rotation events. The exchange will check realtime denylist. Revocation will invalidate both the API key (for acceptance at bridge) and any active short-lived certs via a revocation version header we push to runtime nodes.

sam: Runtime invalidation is tricky. We need a cheap TTL check on servers + a lightweight revocation slot so we don't have to push to all nodes immediately. Could version tokens as `v=<int>` and servers drop tokens with old v when config bumps.

maria: Ops: console UX needs to show which clients are using bridge vs native OIDC. Also send churn metrics (counts, token exchanges/day). devex: can you own the CLI integration?

devex: Yep, we can ship `rw key-migrate` that does the exchange + reconfigures client libs. Plan to include a dry-run mode and explicit consent flow.

security-bot: Note: compliance check — for EU-regulated tenants we need to ensure the bridge doesn't transmit PII outside region. Bridge must be region-aware or run as a private deployment.

eli: We'll add region constraints to the design doc.

julie: Migration timeline idea: Week 0: announce + tools. Week 2: telemetry + warnings on legacy API keys. Week 6: opt-in enforcement for new tenants. Week 12: require bridge exchange for all traffic. Week 20: full deprecation of key acceptance at the control plane. Thoughts?

sam: Seems aggressive but okay if we can automate a lot. Need a rollback cheap path in case partner breakage spikes.

maria: We should also assess client libraries — rotate default auth codepaths to use certs. Keep legacy fallback but flag it as deprecated in logs for 3 months.

eli: Tradeoffs we noted in RFC: Complexity of bridge vs security win of short-lived credentials; partner friction; on-prem/airgap handling. Any objections to moving to an RFC v2 with these specifics and a migration checklist?

julie: No objections. I'll volunteer to own the migration checklist + partner comms.

devex: I'll prototype the CLI and a sample `docker` offline flow for device-assertion by end of sprint.

maria: I'll write the runtime invalidation design doc (token versioning + cheap local cache) and a rollout plan for revocation propagation.

eli: Great. Action items: Julie (comm + checklist), Devex (CLI + sample), Maria (revocation runtime), Sam (device-mode spec), Eli (RFC v2 + sequence diagram). I'll open the follow-up RFC and ping owners. :+1:

sam: One last note — we'll need a test harness for partner migration to avoid surprises. Suggest we create a 'migration canary' tenant and coordinate with a couple of integrators.

eli: Agreed. Adding to RFC v2. Thanks all
